why: This is the base linked-list move with no story: rewire every next pointer to point backwards while walking the list once.
hints: As you walk the list, what do you need to remember so you can point the current node backwards without losing the rest of the list?
Keep three pointers: prev (the already reversed part), cur, and nxt (saved before you overwrite cur.next). Set cur.next = prev, then advance.
One loop until cur is None; prev ends as the new head. O(n) time, O(1) extra space. A recursive version works too but uses O(n) stack.
pitfalls: Save cur.next before overwriting it, or you lose the rest of the list.
The old head must end up pointing to None, which starting with prev = None guarantees.
